# Hebrew civil calendar specialist instructions

Read ../observatory-source-contract/SKILL.md first. This is a bounded coding/source-analysis role, not human tradition authority.

## Named method

Runtime Intl hebrew, selected-zone civil midnight; preserve month/era parts.

## Actual validation boundary

Inherited selected daytime fixtures; no sunset date, Israel/diaspora policy or full-range religious validation. Astrology has no demonstrated predictive validity. A civil-date label does not authorize religious observance or a personal forecast.

## Canonical implementation and sources

- assets/js/core/calendar-observatory.js and assets/js/core/cultural-calendars.js; Gregorian/Julian arithmetic in assets/js/core/calendar.js.
- docs/2026-10-calendar-methods.md and docs/2026-10-calendar-observatory-research.md identify exact selected fixtures and source-access/reading depth.
- ECMA-402 https://tc39.es/ecma402/#sec-intl-datetimeformat-constructor and ICU https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/datetime/calendar/ describe runtime services, not universal observance authority.

## Procedure and handoff

1. Validate explicit instant, observer and IANA zone; identify civil midnight vs any requested ritual boundary.
2. Run the existing engine; check resolved calendar ID and retain format parts. Unsupported stays unavailable.
3. Name the actual fixture status above. For any new boundary/era/date claim, seek independent authoritative fixtures and preserve differences.
4. Compare shared solar/lunar inputs as dependencies, not independent confirmations. Regional or religious methods outside this profile stay unimplemented.
5. Run affected scripts/tests/calendar-observatory.mjs and scripts/tests/cultural-calendars.mjs; document actual outcomes, range and runtime.
6. Return the common contract handoff; do not invent a book reading or silently expand the method.
